entity.name: Imperium42 LLC
entity.description: Imperium42 LLC is a small US software company that builds and maintains Echophrase. In November 2026 we released Echophrase as free, MPL-2.0 open source: no accounts, no subscriptions, no telemetry. Funding goes directly into engineering time and the infrastructure needed to ship signed, trustworthy builds.

projects.name: Echophrase
projects.description: Echophrase is a privacy-first desktop dictation app: press a hotkey, speak, and your words are typed into any app. All speech recognition runs locally on your own GPU or CPU with open models (Parakeet, Qwen3-ASR) through ONNX Runtime, so audio never leaves the machine. It is a free, open alternative to cloud dictation services, and it helps anyone who types less by choice or by necessity, including people with RSI, motor impairments or dyslexia. Built with Rust, Tauri 2 and Svelte. Official signed builds for Windows (DirectML, any DirectX 12 GPU) and Apple Silicon Macs (CoreML/Metal), with community Linux builds.

plans.name: First-class Linux support
plans.description: Bring Linux from community-supported to officially supported: GPU acceleration, Wayland and X11 global hotkeys and text injection across GNOME and KDE, signed packages (Flatpak, AppImage, .deb/.rpm), Linux CI with real end-to-end tests, and auto-updates.

plans.name: Easy NVIDIA CUDA acceleration
plans.description: Make NVIDIA GPU acceleration work out of the box on Windows and Linux: detect the GPU and driver, fetch the matching CUDA execution provider on demand instead of asking users to install toolkits, fall back cleanly to DirectML or CPU, and publish per-GPU benchmarks.

plans.name: Bring-your-own-model out of beta
plans.description: Take custom ONNX speech models from beta to stable: an automated compatibility test suite and accuracy/latency benchmark harness, a public list of verified community models, clearer import errors, and docs for converting models from Hugging Face. This makes Echophrase a local test bed for new open speech models.

plans.name: Localization and accessibility
plans.description: Translate the interface into more languages with a community translation platform (beyond English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese), validate and tune multilingual recognition models per language, and run an accessibility pass: full keyboard navigation, screen reader support and hands-free operation for users who cannot type.

plans.name: Signed builds and security
plans.description: Yearly costs of trustworthy releases: Windows code signing, Apple notarization, macOS and Windows CI runners, update hosting, test hardware across GPU vendors, and an independent security review of the app and its updater.

plans.name: Community support
plans.description: Any amount helps cover maintenance: bug fixes, model updates and keeping up with Windows and macOS changes.
